item.text: {"gaps":[{"concept":"SRY activates SOX9, which drives Sertoli cell differentiation and testis cord formation.","why_tested":"An SRY-positive embryo has a SOX9 defect and fails to develop testes.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"SRY translocation onto the X chromosome can produce a 46,XX individual with testes and a male phenotype.","why_tested":"A phenotypic male has a 46,XX karyotype and an SRY-positive X chromosome.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Complete 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis (Swyer syndrome) causes streak gonads, a uterus, female external genitalia, and absent spontaneous puberty.","why_tested":"Primary amenorrhea and little breast development occur in an adolescent with a uterus and 46,XY karyotype.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Complete androgen insensitivity is an X-linked androgen receptor defect: 46,XY, testes, absent uterus, blind vagina, breasts, and scant pubic hair.","why_tested":"Primary amenorrhea with breasts, scant pubic hair, and inguinal testes must be distinguished from Müllerian agenesis.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Androgen insensitivity typically produces male-range or elevated testosterone and elevated LH because androgen-mediated negative feedback is impaired.","why_tested":"Hormone results distinguish androgen resistance from impaired testosterone synthesis in a 46,XY patient.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Partial androgen insensitivity can cause ambiguous genitalia, severe hypospadias, and pubertal gynecomastia.","why_tested":"A 46,XY adolescent with hypospadias and gynecomastia has residual androgen receptor activity.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Autosomal recessive SRD5A2 deficiency causes undervirilized external genitalia despite testes, Wolffian structures, and Müllerian regression; virilization occurs at puberty.","why_tested":"A child raised as female develops a deeper voice and phallic enlargement at puberty.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"5α-reductase deficiency produces a high testosterone-to-DHT ratio and usually lacks the pubertal gynecomastia characteristic of partial androgen insensitivity.","why_tested":"Hormone results and pubertal findings distinguish two causes of 46,XY undervirilization.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"AMH or AMH-receptor defects cause persistent Müllerian duct syndrome: a phenotypic male retains a uterus and may have cryptorchidism.","why_tested":"A uterus is discovered during surgery for an undescended testis in a 46,XY child.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Prenatal androgen excess from 21-hydroxylase deficiency virilizes 46,XX external genitalia while ovaries and Müllerian internal structures remain intact.","why_tested":"A newborn has ambiguous external genitalia, no palpable testes, and a uterus.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Placental aromatase deficiency can virilize both a 46,XX fetus and the pregnant mother.","why_tested":"Maternal hirsutism accompanies ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XX newborn.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Placental hCG stimulates fetal Leydig cell testosterone production during male sexual differentiation.","why_tested":"A stem asks which placental hormone supports fetal androgen production.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"INSL3 promotes transabdominal testicular descent; androgen signaling supports subsequent passage through the inguinal canal into the scrotum.","why_tested":"A defect in a descent signal leaves testes undescended despite otherwise normal duct development.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Cryptorchidism is more common with prematurity and increases infertility and testicular germ cell tumor risk.","why_tested":"An undescended inguinal testis is linked to later impaired fertility or malignancy.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"During inguinal descent, testes acquire internal spermatic fascia from transversalis fascia, cremasteric fascia from internal oblique, and external spermatic fascia from external oblique.","why_tested":"A stem asks which abdominal wall layer supplies a spermatic cord covering.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Failed processus vaginalis closure causes communicating hydrocele, a usually painless, transilluminating scrotal swelling.","why_tested":"A newborn’s scrotal swelling transilluminates and communicates with the peritoneal cavity.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"A patent processus vaginalis also permits congenital indirect inguinal hernia, with bowel entering the scrotum through the deep inguinal ring.","why_tested":"A reducible infant scrotal mass contains bowel instead of hydrocele fluid.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Mesonephric tubules form efferent ductules connecting the rete testis to the epididymis.","why_tested":"A question asks the embryologic origin of the ducts between testis and epididymis.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"The appendix testis is a Müllerian remnant; its torsion can produce a tender blue-dot sign.","why_tested":"A child with acute scrotal pain has a blue spot near the superior testicular pole.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"The urogenital sinus gives rise to prostatic and bulbourethral gland epithelium in males and vestibular and paraurethral gland epithelium in females.","why_tested":"A question asks the embryologic source of accessory genital gland epithelium.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Most male urethral epithelium derives from urogenital sinus endoderm; distal glanular urethral epithelium derives from surface ectoderm.","why_tested":"A stem asks which embryologic tissue forms the distal penile urethra.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"A septate uterus has a normal outer fundal contour; a bicornuate uterus has a deep external fundal cleft.","why_tested":"Pelvic imaging shows two uterine cavities, requiring distinction between failed septum resorption and failed duct fusion.","yield":"hi"},{"concept":"Uterus didelphys commonly has two cervices and may have a longitudinal vaginal septum.","why_tested":"Examination finds duplicated cervices alongside two separate uterine cavities.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"A unicornuate uterus results from absent or arrested development of one Müllerian duct and may include a rudimentary horn.","why_tested":"Imaging shows one uterine horn with a small contralateral remnant.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Gartner duct cysts occur along the anterolateral vaginal wall.","why_tested":"A vaginal wall cyst must be identified by its location and Wolffian origin.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Imperforate hymen reflects failed hymenal canalization; transverse vaginal septum reflects failed fusion or canalization between vaginal components.","why_tested":"An obstructed vagina has cyclic pain, but examination distinguishes a bulging hymen from a higher vaginal septum.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Vaginal atresia can result from failed development or canalization of the sinovaginal bulbs.","why_tested":"A patient has congenital lower vaginal absence despite developed Müllerian structures.","yield":"mid"},{"concept":"Fetal exposure to 5α-reductase inhibitors such as finasteride can impair development of male external genitalia.","why_tested":"A medication exposure during pregnancy is linked to undervirilized genitalia in a male fetus.","yield":"mid"}]}
